sections.h2: What Is the UAE E-Invoicing Mandate?

paragraphs.text: Under UAE electronic invoicing, the UAE is replacing PDF and paper tax invoices with structured electronic invoices for most business-to-business and business-to-government sales. Invoices travel between accredited service providers (ASPs) on a Peppol-based network, and invoice data is reported to the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) at the same time. Large businesses must go live on 1 January 2027, and other VAT-registered businesses on 1 July 2027.

paragraphs.html: For ERPNext users, ERPNext e-invoicing UAE compliance means your system must produce invoice data in the UAE standard, send it to your ASP and record the result. Our UAE e-invoicing compliance work covers all three. For official guidance, see the UAE Ministry of Finance and the Federal Tax Authority.

sections.h2: When Does Your Business Need to Comply?
rows: Revenue of AED 50 million or more

paragraphs.text: If your business is in the first group, the ASP deadline has passed and go-live is weeks away. If you are in the second group, now is the right time to start. UAE e-invoicing 2027 projects that begin early have time for clean data, proper testing and staff training. An ERPNext UAE e-invoicing project typically takes 6–10 weeks from review to live sending.

sections.h2: How the UAE E-Invoicing Model Works
sections.intro: The UAE uses a five-corner model built on Peppol:

items.title: Corner 1
items.text: Your ERPNext system creates the invoice.

items.title: Corner 2
items.text: Your ASP checks it, converts it to the UAE format and sends it.

items.title: Corner 4
items.text: The buyer's system receives the invoice.

items.title: Corner 5
items.text: Invoice data is reported to the FTA.

paragraphs.text: Peppol e-invoicing ERPNext setups handle corner 1 and the link to corner 2. The UAE format is based on the Peppol PINT AE specification, so ERPNext PINT AE data must be complete and correct before your ASP can send it.

Because both sides use the same network, buyers receive invoices straight into their own systems, which speeds up approvals and payment. For your finance team, that usually means fewer calls asking for a copy of an invoice and fewer disputes over what was billed.

sections.h2: How Does ERPNext Connect to the UAE System?
sections.intro: ERPNext does not send invoices to the FTA directly. Instead, ERPNext ASP integration connects your invoices to your chosen accredited provider through its API. ERPNext Peppol integration then follows four steps:
rows: Sales invoice submitted with all required fields
Structured invoice data sent to your ASP automatically
The ASP checks the data and returns accepted or rejected
The result is saved on the invoice, with errors flagged

paragraphs.text: ERPNext Peppol UAE connections work for invoices and credit notes alike. ERPNext ASP UAE setup includes credentials, test and live endpoints and a log of every message, so you can prove what was sent and when. This UAE e-invoicing integration keeps your team working in ERPNext as usual. Our ERPNext FTA e-invoicing setups follow FTA and Ministry of Finance guidance as it is updated.

rows: ERPNext version, VAT setup, invoice types and data quality
Compare providers and appoint one before your deadline
Customer TRNs, addresses, item codes and tax categories
Add and map every required invoice field
Link ERPNext to the ASP's API, test and live
Invoices, credit notes, exports and edge cases
Switch on live sending and watch results

paragraphs.text: This UAE e-invoicing setup keeps billing running throughout. During testing, your team keeps issuing normal invoices while we send copies to the provider's test environment, so nothing changes for customers until the live switch. Our UAE e-invoicing implementation includes written documentation of every field and mapping. Each UAE e-invoicing project ends with a sign-off from your finance team.

Every business must appoint its own accredited service provider, and the choice affects cost, reliability and support for years. When comparing providers, check their fees per invoice or per month, how their API handles errors and retries, whether they support credit notes and exports fully, and how quickly they respond in UAE hours. ERPNext e-invoice UAE connections are similar across providers, so we stay neutral and help you compare. A good ERPNext UAE e-invoicing partner should explain these trade-offs before you sign with anyone.

UAE e-invoices carry more structured data than a typical PDF invoice. Common gaps we fix include missing buyer TRNs, incomplete addresses, unclear item descriptions, missing tax category codes and inconsistent units of measure. Fixing these before go-live is the single biggest factor in avoiding rejected invoices, which is why every ERPNext UAE e-invoicing project we run starts here. UAE e-invoicing readiness therefore starts with your customer and item masters, not with the connection itself.

Some invoices need extra care. Sales to customers outside the UAE, sales to government entities, invoices between free zone and mainland companies, and deemed supplies each carry different data. Self-billing arrangements and invoices with mixed tax rates need their own checks too. We list every invoice type your business issues, then test each one with your provider. Any ERPNext UAE e-invoicing project that skips these cases risks rejections in the first month.

Every invoice sent, every response from your provider and every correction stays linked in ERPNext, with timestamps. Your accountant and the FTA can trace any invoice from creation to acceptance. Good ERPNext e-invoicing compliance UAE practice also means reviewing rejected invoices weekly in the first months, which our ERPNext UAE e-invoicing support includes.

sections.h2: What Happens If You Miss Your Deadline?
sections.intro: Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025 sets administrative penalties once your phase begins, including:

items.text: AED 5,000 per month for not implementing e-invoicing or not appointing an ASP on time
AED 100 per invoice or credit note not issued electronically, capped at AED 5,000 per month
AED 1,000 per day for not notifying the FTA of a system failure, or not updating your ASP with changed company details

outro.text: These amounts add up quickly for busy businesses, which is why starting your ERPNext UAE e-invoicing project early costs far less than being late.

paragraphs.text: UAE e-invoicing for SMEs follows the same rules as for large companies, just six months later. Free zone companies, mainland companies, exporters and businesses selling to government entities all need to plan. ERPNext e-invoicing Dubai and ERPNext e-invoicing Abu Dhabi projects follow the same process, whatever the emirate. The UAE e-invoicing mandate applies to VAT-registered businesses across all seven emirates. Our UAE e-invoicing phases planning makes sure each group company starts on the right date. Groups often have one company above the AED 50 million line and others below it, so each entity may go live six months apart. We plan both dates from the start, so the second launch reuses everything built for the first.

items.a: Businesses with revenue of AED 50 million or more go live on 1 January 2027. Others go live on 1 July 2027, and must appoint an accredited service provider by 31 March 2027. Government entities follow on 1 October 2027.

ERPNext can produce the structured invoice data the UAE system needs and connect to an accredited service provider through its API. We add the required fields, clean your data and test the connection before go-live.

items.q: Do we need a service provider?
items.a: Yes. UAE e-invoices must be sent through an accredited service provider. ERPNext connects to the provider you appoint, and we help you compare options.

items.q: What happens if we are late?
items.a: Penalties include AED 5,000 per month for not implementing e-invoicing or not appointing a provider on time, and AED 100 per invoice not issued electronically, capped at AED 5,000 per month.
Yes. Credit notes follow the same e-invoicing rules as invoices. We set up and test credit notes, partial returns and corrections before go-live.

items.q: Is this different from ZATCA in Saudi Arabia?
items.a: Yes. Saudi Arabia's ZATCA uses direct clearance with the tax authority, while the UAE uses accredited service providers on a Peppol network. Our uae e-invoicing erpnext setups follow UAE rules, and our ERPNext ZATCA e-invoicing service covers Saudi requirements. Many people search for "UAE einvoicing" help without knowing the difference, so we explain it in the first call.

Most ERPNext users need 6–10 weeks, depending on data quality and the number of companies. Starting three to six months before your go-live date leaves time for proper testing. Every UAE e-invoicing training session for your team is included.
